chapter: New Orleans pianists and Clarence Williams
title: Willis, Spencer Williams, Texas pianists and McNamara
summary: A white pianist named Willis at the Shields house, Spencer Williams, Galveston pianists, and the harmonically inventive McNamara.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: That's right. He was on that record too. That's right, Arthur Campbell. And he was a good piano player. Now these fellas would play piano during those times. They had so many of them that I could name, but they wasn't the really top piano players. Now we had another piano player play good, a white boy played piano, was a very good piano player during that time. He was some kin to Shields, to Larry Shields, the trumpet player. Well they used to, I don't know if it was his cousin or what, but they used to live at Thood and Clara. And all the bands used to be on the wagon, used to stop and go in their house, and on Sundays they used to have jam sessions there all the time. The Shields? The Shields, yeah. And they had a piano player used to go there, out their house and play all the time. His name was, his name was Willis. His name was Willis. He was a very good piano player and he moved, he left here and went to California and he died. And Steve Lewis and this Shields, his cousin or brothers, he was playing in Storyville at that time.
Well there's another white pianist I've heard of, Kid Ross I believe. Did you know him? No. I think he played at Lula White's house for a while.
No I didn't know him. I know Lula White's nephew.
Spencer Williams, yeah. I know him. I saw him in New York too.
He was supposed to live I believe in Sweden or Norway or something like that.
Yeah, he's living over there but he comes to the states every year, sometimes twice a year. And I happened to see him by Mills on Broadway, Broadway 49.
Another pianist, when you were talking about Galveston and that part of Texas, did you ever run into Lazy Daddy over there? Yeah. Fillmore I guess. Yeah, yeah. How was he?

I never got to know him. But he was a good piano player, yeah, he was good. I know him and I know a fellow called Jimmy Prye, he was another pretty good piano player around that way. And there's another piano player who is living the day, was a very famous piano player among all the piano players because they used to go sit in the show to listen at him play. They used to listen to the guys that didn't read, used to listen at him to catch tunes for him. I mean he was a piano player with use of a lot of harmony and that was McNamara. Yeah, he plays, I think he's on, I think he plays with this band WDSU. He played organ too. He used to play, he used to play the organ at the Lowest State and then he played piano. His name, Mac Mamamara I think his name is. Yeah. He's very, very, of course if you hear him now you can tell he used to get piano right today, but he was good then. I think he played with this Don Busters.
Yeah, he used to play with, when Al Huyte was playing with him.
